Posted September 10, 2005
Analysis by Richard Cowan

After Canadas Parliamentary elections last year, Prime Minister Paul Martin said that his government was committed to marijuana decriminalization and would  reintroduce the legislation that had died with the previous Parliament. That much they did do, but as usual, that is as far as it got.
See
 Cannabis Reform and The Canadian Election. (Its Okay to Exhale, and I Promise that Your Eyes Wont Glaze Over.)

Earlier this week, the parliamentary secretary to Justice Minister Irwin Cotler said  the government will delay it again until after elections in January. "We are still committed to [decrim] but it's a question of time., he said. Yeah, sure.
(The current Liberal government did not win have a majority in last years election, and the PM promised to hold an early election as soon as a report on a major political scandal is published.)

They have been playing this game for years.
From 2003, see
 Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon  Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.
and
 Canadian Prime Minister Says He Has Been In Favor Of Decrim Since 1980. How Time Flies When You Are In Power. Possession Law Hostage to Medical Cannabis. Another Deadline On Taking Care of Patients.

The process is complicated by the Liberals need to pose as brave, bold and ever-so-progressive and pretend that they are defying the US. Canadians like to joke about how ignorant Americans are about Canada, but they display a dangerous ignorance about their giant neighbor.
See
 Decrim Okay With Drug Czar Walters? A Gaffe or a Miracle? Lessons for Canada.They Should Also Notice Alaska.

One problem with passing the bill this session was that it would attract so many witnesses that they would not have time to ignore them all and then pass the bill anyway. Of course, the bill would have to go to the Senate, where a committee issued a 700 page report calling for legalization in 2002.
See Canadian Senate report

I say that the government would ignore the witnesses because they have admitted that they did not even read the Senate report before writing their phony decrim bill. As one might gather, I think that Canada is better off without this fraud.  

Of course, opponents of even decrim claim that not arresting adults will cause more children to use marijuana. However, prohibition has not exactly been a rousing success in that regard. In 2002, an estimated 12.2 per cent of Canadians admitted to smoking marijuana - up from 6.5 per cent in 1989, according to Statistics Canada.

Moreover, in the US there has never been any correlation between the levels of cannabis use and the state laws on possession. This week NORML reported that downgrading of cannabis to a non-arrestable offense has not been associated with an increase in adolescents' use of the drug, according to survey data published by the United Kingdom's Department of Health.

The Department found that the number of young people who admitted having consumed cannabis in the past year fell from 13 percent to 11 percent in 2004 - the first reported dip in four years.

In January of 2004, Britain downgraded marijuana from a Class B to a Class C scheduled drug. Under this reclassification, individuals found in possession of personal use amounts of marijuana are cautioned by police, but, in general, are no longer arrested. (Police do retain the discretion to make an arrest under special "aggravated" circumstances, such as if marijuana is smoked on school grounds.)

This report contradicts the prohibitionist party line so it too must go into the memory hole, along with the Canadian Senate report. (The prohibitionist memory hole has an infinite capacity.
See
 Health Canada Escalates Its War on the Sick and Dying as the Canadian Cannabis War Heats Up. Challenges Set In the BC Courts
and
 Teens See Marijuana As Less Harmful Than Cigarettes. Oh, The Horror! Is Health Canada Dangerous to the Health of Canadas Teens?

While I think that Canada is better off with the current possession laws than a new one that pretends to be something that it isnt, the same cannot be said for its so-called medical marijuana access program.

The sad fact is that, despite plans to make cannabis available in pharmacies and allowing some patients to grow their own (with seeds from Marc Emery or someone else who would supposedly be breaking Canadian law??), most Canadians who need medical cannabis are no better off than patients in (parts of) California or some of the other states with medical cannabis laws. The failure of Health Canada to obey court orders to provide a workable medical access program remains a threat to all of the cannabis laws.
See
 Philippe Lucas Analysis of the Consequences of Health Canadas Failure to Obey the Ontario Courts Ruling On Medical Cannabis. Is Cannabis Legal in Canada?
and
 The Paupers of Pot and the Politics of Cannabis Prohibition In Canada. The Other Cases Raise Questions That Canada Must Answer. Will Canada Murder Michelle Rainey?

Also, it is worth noting that Health Canadas approval of Sativex has done little for patients. It is simply too expensive and hard to get for most patients. On the other hand, its approval should silence those who claim that the medical value of cannabis has not been approved by the (infallible) government.
See
 Program notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report June 23, 2005 Feds Raid SF Clubs. Sativex in Canada, High Price. Oaksterdam Okays Vaporization; BC Tests Cannabis. Marijuana Raids Reignite Zapatistas

To make matters worse, Canada is collaborating with the DEA in a way that endangers American medical cannabis patients. NOW Magazine http://www.nowtoronto.com/ reports that The DEA denies it, but suspicious pot activists suggest it's planning a mass roundup of Emery's buyers.

Unfortunately, things may be even worse than I reported last month.
See
 DEA Tries To Scam Emery Customers Into Admitting That They Were Buying Seeds.

NOW says, info the DEA has so far disclosed to (Emerys) lawyer, John Conroy, indicates that its agents scanned both the incoming and outgoing mail for his seed operation in the weeks prior to his arrest on July 29.

Spokespeople with neither the DEA nor the U.S.  Department of Justice in Seattle, Washington, could - or would - shed any light on this caper.

Ditto for RCMP spokesperson Paul Marsh, who refers all questions on the matter to Foreign Affairs in Ottawa, which did not return calls.

Seattle-based prosecutor Todd Greenberg is a little more forthcoming.

"They're trying to make people angry against their government and the U.S.  government," he says of the alleged DEA sting, before saying there could be further arrests.
See
 Baghdad on The Bayou. Chernobyl for the American Political Class. Changing the Context for the Drugwar. How Damaging This Fiasco Must Be To The Morale Of Our Troops In Iraq.

Ian Hillman at the U.S. Consulate in Vancouver, suggests just how large the Emery probe has become, saying, This nearly involves every state.  There are aspects of the investigation where it's not in our interest to reveal how many people are working on it.  [But] I understand it involves dozens of people on both sides of the border.

In other words, Canadas collaboration with the DEA has put a number of American patients in danger of being arrested under US federal marijuana laws that will not allow the patients even to suggest that they have a medical problem that they might be treating with cannabis. 

I think that it would be very unwise for anyone in DEAland to buy seeds by mail from Canada, or perhaps even the UK for that matter. A doctor in the Midwest was arrested earlier this year with about 30 plants that he was growing with seeds traced when they were shipped from the UK. The Dutch seed producers generally do not ship to the US, but they will sell to (discrete) Americans who go to The Netherlands to buy.

This is not the first time that Canada has betrayed a medical cannabis patient over seeds. Ironically, when Steve Tuck first came to Canada in June of 2001, he donated 15,000 medical cannabis seeds, of 400 different varieties, to Health Canada. It was not until after he gave them these seeds that he had to flee DEAland in fear of his life. However, in all of his refugee hearings, the government of Canada has tried to ignore their obligation to Tuck, just as they have ignored every inconvenient fact about cannabis. And Canada continues to try to expel both Tuck and the Kubbys, despite overwhelming evidence of illegal activity by both California and DEAland federal law enforcement.
See
 Placer County, Still Murderous After All These Years. Kubbys Find Secret Death Warrant Signed by Disqualified Judge. Key To Canadian Refuge, If Not Justice In California.

Consequently, it is hardly surprising that Canada has betrayed both American and Canadian medical cannabis patients. With its decrim bill delayed again, its medical cannabis program shambolic, and with Canadian narks collaborating with DEAland, there is a greater need  and opportunity  than ever for a real debate on cannabis prohibition in Canada and the rest of the world.
See
 Jamaican Attorney General Wants Debate On Implementing Decriminalization  So Does The Canadian Justice Minister. Why Isnt There An International Debate? Analysis by Richard Cowan
